pages.text: The three struct types of the library. Declare variables of them like of any struct, e.g. $(1)VARIABLE spot STRUCT c0de/minecraft/POSITION$().

$(l)POSITION$() is a block: $(1)x$(), $(1)y$() and $(1)z$() are INTEGERs, $(1)dimension$() is a STRING. In every function, an empty $(1)dimension$() means the dimension of the trigger block. Otherwise it holds an ID like $(1)minecraft:the_nether$(); an unknown ID raises INVALID_ARGUMENT.

$(l)ENTITY$() is an entity found by FIND_ENTITIES: $(1)uuid$() (STRING, for TELEPORT), $(1)type$() (STRING, like $(1)minecraft:sheep$()), $(1)name$() (STRING) and $(1)position$() (POSITION). The name is the name of a player, the name from a name tag, or else the name of the type.

The $(1)position$() of an ENTITY is the block the entity is in: its coordinates are rounded down, so x = -0.5 is block -1. Its $(1)dimension$() is empty in the dimension of the trigger block. Compare $(1)type$(), not $(1)name$(): a name can be in the language of the game.
$(l)ITEM_STACK$() is one slot of an inventory, from GET_INVENTORY: $(1)id$() (STRING, like $(1)minecraft:wheat$()) and $(1)count$() (INTEGER). An empty slot has the id "" and the count 0.
$(1)VARIABLE spot STRUCT c0de/minecraft/POSITION$(br)BEGIN$(br)  x 10$(br)  y 64$(br)  z -20$(br)END VARIABLE$()
$(1)dimension$() is left out, so it stays empty: the dimension of the trigger block.
